function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

Root cause found and fixed: in sqlparse/filters/reindent.py, ReindentFilter._next_token had an inverted condition (`if not (token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN')`) that caused it to recurse into itself with `idx=None` whenever the token found was NOT 'BETWEEN' (the common case), rather than only when it WAS 'BETWEEN' (the intended BETWEEN...AND skip logic). This led to `tlist.token_next_by(idx=None)` doing `idx += 1` on None, raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +=: 'NoneType' and 'int'`. This broke sqlparse.format(..., reindent=True) entirely, cascading into 41 failing checks (CLI formatting, reindent-based tests, etc.).

Fix: corrected the condition to `if token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN':` so recursion only happens to skip past the AND in a BETWEEN...AND pair, and otherwise the found split-keyword token is returned immediately as intended.

Verified via `check`: 41 passing, 0 failing.

Changed `if not (token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN'):` to `if token and token.normalized == 'BETWEEN':` so the BETWEEN...AND skip logic only triggers for actual BETWEEN tokens, and other split keywords are returned directly. This restores correct behavior for sqlparse.format(reindent=True) and all downstream CLI/formatting functionality.
